seed: Where the words sit DOWN a box. A text box is stored a few points taller than its words, all of that room past the bottom edge, and every box a person sees has it taken off again. Centre the STORED box in a control and the label lands two points above the middle of it. This walk drops the two starters whose labels moved, and then shows the Down row of the Text section on a plain text box, where the pictures say something else worth knowing: a text box on the canvas is always exactly as tall as its words, so Top, Middle and Bottom have no room to move anything and nothing happens when they are pressed.

steps.note: THE TEST: a Badge, a Button and a Nav Bar. The Badge's count and the Button's word used to sit two points above the middle of the pill they are in, because the control centred the stored text box rather than the words in it. Look at the room above and below each word.
a plain text box, selected. Its outline sits on the words: H in Position & Size is the height of the words and there is no room in it to move them.

WHAT THIS SHOWS: Middle is now the chosen segment in Down, and the words have not moved a point, because a box its own size has nowhere to move them. Down only bites when something else gives the box room, which today means a container stretching it.
